display.title: Episode 277: Judge for a Day, Chapter 2 (Before Shavuos)
display.summary_short: A week before Shavuos: why every Jew, even a baby, should hear the Ten Commandments in shul, a Havdalah phone quiz, and a children's pretend court that gives a real judge the clue he needs.
display.summary_long: Broadcast one week before Erev Shavuos 5747. Uncle Yossi describes the reading of the Aseres HaDibros on the first day of Shavuos, when the whole shul falls silent and we again stand before Hashem in awe and say 'Naaseh v'nishma'. He gives the Yom Tov candle time and brachos and urges every child to come to shul and to bring relatives and friends, even babies, since every Jew was at Har Sinai, and to fill out the Shavuos mitzvah chart. Mitzvah Time reviews Havdalah, and a girl answers the phone quiz and wins a Havdalah candle. A Boro Park Beis Yaakov class recites the Shema. Story time continues 'Judge for a Day': visiting Berel's shop, Leibel spots wood shavings and a hole in the thin wall to Ivan's shop, which explains how Ivan knew about the hidden coins, but how can it be proven? Meanwhile the worried judge, strolling in the park, secretly watches children act out the case, and their little judge proposes a test with a pail of warm water that makes the real judge leap for joy. The final chapter is promised for next week.
display.lesson: Every Jew, young and old, should come to shul on Shavuos to hear the Ten Commandments and receive the Torah anew with joy.
